kept_evidence.summary: A Morgan Stanley Research bill-of-materials analysis cited by MarketScale estimates that NVIDIA's Vera Rubin VR200 NVL72 rack will cost hyperscale cloud providers about $7.8 million per unit, up from roughly $4 million for the current GB300 NVL72 generation, with NVIDIA estimated to charge about $55,000 per Rubin GPU and $5,000 per Vera CPU when sold in volume; Morgan Stanley notes that a hyperscaler self-sourcing certain memory modules could bring the rack price down to about $6.7 million.

Morgan Stanley puts memory content per Vera Rubin VR200 NVL72 rack at about $2 million, a 435% jump from the prior generation, driven by a threefold increase in LPDDR5X capacity to 54 terabytes per rack plus roughly $1 million or more in 3D NAND storage; memory's share of the bill of materials rose from 5–10% on the GB200 to 25–30% on the VR200, while the GPU's share fell from roughly 63% to 51%.

Morgan Stanley's bill-of-materials analysis cited by MarketScale says NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 first shipments are scheduled for the third quarter of 2026, with volume ramping in the fourth quarter of 2026.

MarketScale reports that constrained supply of DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory against AI-driven demand is raising component costs across the market, that contract DDR5 pricing has climbed sharply, and that device makers including Samsung and Apple are expected to pass higher memory costs into upcoming products, tying the AI buildout and consumer-device memory prices to the same supply squeeze.
